course.title: Hospitality and Customer Service
course.tagline: Serve guests so well they return: manners, complaints and five-star habits.

days.title: What Is Hospitality?
days.goal: Know what hospitality means and why it matters.

video.title: Hotel & Restaurant Problem Handling | Guest Complaints & Service Recovery

steps: Hospitality means making guests feel welcome and cared for.
Service is what you do. Hospitality is how you make people feel.
Good hospitality brings guests back. Bad service drives them away.
Every worker matters: the cleaner, the cook, the server, and the manager.
A smile, a greeting, and care are the start of great service.
days.task: Write down what hospitality means to you in one sentence.
days.challenge: Visit a hotel or restaurant and note one good and one bad service moment.

quiz.q: What is hospitality?
options: Making guests feel welcome and cared for
quiz.explain: Hospitality is making guests feel welcome and cared for.

quiz.q: What is the difference between service and hospitality?
options: Service is what you do. Hospitality is how you make people feel
quiz.explain: Service is the task. Hospitality is the feeling you create.

quiz.q: Who matters in hospitality?
options: Every worker, from cleaner to manager
quiz.explain: Every worker shapes the guest's experience.

days.title: Welcoming Guests: The First 10 Seconds
days.goal: Welcome guests so they feel valued at once.

video.title: HOW TO: Welcome a guest at your hotel

steps: Stand up straight and smile when a guest arrives.
Make eye contact and greet them within 10 seconds.
Use a warm greeting: 'Good morning, welcome. How can I help you?'
Use the guest's name if you know it.
Listen to what they need before you speak.
days.task: Practise greeting a friend as if they are a guest.
days.challenge: Practise three greetings: morning, afternoon, and evening.

quiz.q: How fast should you greet a guest?
quiz.explain: A fast greeting makes guests feel welcome at once.

quiz.q: Why use the guest's name?
options: It makes them feel valued and known
quiz.explain: Using a name makes service feel personal.

quiz.q: Why listen before you speak?
options: So you understand what the guest really needs
quiz.explain: Listening first helps you help the guest properly.

days.title: The Front Desk: Check-In Step by Step
days.goal: Check a guest in smoothly at a hotel.

video.title: Hotel & Restaurant Problem Resolution | Handle Complaints & Win Back Guest Trust

steps: Greet the guest and ask for their name and booking.
Check the booking on your system or book.
Ask for ID if your hotel needs it.
Give them the room key and explain the room number, breakfast time, and Wi-Fi.
Wish them a good stay and offer help with bags.
days.task: Practise a check-in with a friend playing the guest.
days.challenge: Write a check-in checklist you can use at work.

quiz.q: What is the first step at check-in?
options: Greet the guest and ask for their name and booking
quiz.explain: Greet first, then ask for the name and booking.

quiz.q: What should you explain at check-in?
options: Room number, breakfast time, and Wi-Fi
quiz.explain: Guests need the room number, breakfast time, and Wi-Fi details.

quiz.q: Why offer help with bags?
options: It shows care and makes the guest feel welcome
quiz.explain: Helping with bags is a small act that makes a big impression.

days.title: Serving Food: The Right Way
days.goal: Serve food and drinks in a restaurant the professional way.

video.title: How to Handle Hotel Guest Complaints | 4 Essential Front Office Lessons

steps: Serve from the left side of the guest. Clear from the right.
Hold plates flat. Do not tilt them.
Serve ladies and older guests first.
Never reach across a guest. Walk around instead.
Check back within 2 minutes: 'Is everything alright?'
days.task: Practise serving a meal to a friend, step by step.
days.challenge: Practise carrying two plates safely.

quiz.q: Which side do you serve from?
quiz.explain: Serve from the left. Clear from the right.

quiz.q: Why not reach across a guest?
quiz.explain: Reaching across a guest is rude and makes them uncomfortable.

quiz.q: Why check back within 2 minutes?
quiz.explain: Checking back early lets you fix problems before guests get unhappy.

days.title: Silver Service: Fine Dining Basics
days.goal: Learn the basics of silver service.

video.title: Rapport Hospitality Customer Service Demo: How to Handle a Frustrated Hotel Guest

steps: Silver service is formal table service with serving dishes and tongs.
Hold the serving dish in your left hand and serve with your right.
Serve small amounts. Guests can ask for more.
Keep your back straight and move calmly.
Clear plates only when everyone at the table has finished.
days.task: Practise silver service at home with a plate and tongs.
days.challenge: Serve a meal to your family using silver service steps.

quiz.q: What is silver service?
options: Formal table service with serving dishes and tongs
quiz.explain: Silver service is formal service using dishes and tongs.

quiz.q: When do you clear plates?
options: When everyone at the table has finished
quiz.explain: Clearing only when all have finished is polite and professional.

quiz.q: Why move calmly in fine dining?
options: Calm movement looks professional and relaxes guests
quiz.explain: Calm, smooth movement makes guests feel relaxed.

days.title: Talking to Guests: Words That Help
days.goal: Use kind, clear words with guests.

video.title: How to Handle Restaurant Complaints

steps: Speak clearly and slowly. Smile when you talk.
Use polite words: 'please', 'thank you', 'of course'.
Avoid slang with guests you do not know well.
If you do not know the answer, say: 'Let me check for you.'
Never argue with a guest. Stay calm and kind.
days.task: Practise three polite phrases with a friend.
days.challenge: Write a list of words to use and words to avoid with guests.

quiz.q: What should you say if you do not know the answer?
quiz.explain: 'Let me check' shows you care and will find the answer.

quiz.q: Why avoid slang with guests?
options: Polite, clear words suit all guests
quiz.explain: Clear, polite words work for every guest.

quiz.q: Why never argue with a guest?
options: Arguing makes the guest angrier and hurts your business
quiz.explain: Arguing never helps. Staying calm solves problems.

days.title: Week 1 Project: Serve a Meal Like a Pro
days.goal: Serve a full meal to guests, from greeting to goodbye.

video.title: Complaint Handling

steps: Greet guests warmly when they arrive.
Seat them, offer water, and present the menu.
Take orders, repeat them back, and serve food correctly.
Check back within 2 minutes and fix any problem.
Clear plates, offer dessert, and thank guests as they leave.
days.task: Serve a full meal to your household as if in a restaurant.
days.challenge: Ask your guests what felt good and what to improve.

quiz.q: What are the steps of service?
options: Greet, seat, order, serve, check back, clear, thank
quiz.explain: Service is greet, seat, order, serve, check back, clear, and thank.

quiz.q: Why repeat orders back?
quiz.explain: Repeating orders stops mistakes.

quiz.q: Why thank guests as they leave?
options: So they feel valued and come back
quiz.explain: A warm goodbye makes guests want to return.

project.title: Serve a Meal Like a Pro
project.brief: Serve a full meal from greeting to goodbye.
checks: Food served correctly, from the left

days.title: Handling Complaints: Listen and Fix
days.goal: Handle a guest complaint calmly and well.

video.title: Silver Service Training

steps: Listen first. Let the guest finish speaking.
Say sorry, even if it is not your fault.
Ask what would make it right.
Fix it fast: replace the dish, offer a discount, or give a free drink.
Thank them for telling you.
days.task: Practise handling a complaint with a friend playing the guest.
days.challenge: Write a short guide for handling complaints.

quiz.q: What is the first step with a complaint?
quiz.explain: Listening first shows respect and helps you understand the problem.

quiz.q: Why say sorry?
options: It shows you care about the guest
quiz.explain: An apology calms the guest and shows you care.

quiz.q: What can you offer to fix a complaint?
options: A replacement dish, a discount, or a free drink
quiz.explain: A replacement, discount, or free drink can turn a bad visit into a good one.

days.title: Service Recovery: Win Guests Back
days.goal: Turn an unhappy guest into a loyal one.

video.title: How to Service Food & Beverages | Restaurants | Hotels | Waiter | Fine Dining Training Video

steps: Service recovery means fixing a problem so well the guest returns.
Act fast. A quick fix matters more than a perfect one.
Give a little extra: a free dessert or a sincere apology.
Follow up: ask if everything is alright now.
Tell your manager what happened so it does not happen again.
days.task: Practise a service recovery with a friend.
days.challenge: Write down three ways to win back an unhappy guest.

quiz.q: What is service recovery?
options: Fixing a problem so well the guest returns
quiz.explain: Service recovery turns a bad experience into a reason to return.

quiz.q: Why act fast?
options: A quick fix matters more than a perfect one
quiz.explain: Fast action shows you care. Waiting makes guests angrier.

quiz.q: Why tell your manager?
options: So the problem does not happen again
quiz.explain: Reporting problems helps the whole team improve.

days.title: Difficult Guests: Stay Calm
days.goal: Handle difficult guests without losing your cool.

video.title: How to Handle Customer Complaints in Your Restaurant?

steps: Stay calm. Speak slowly and softly.
Do not take it personally. The guest is unhappy with the situation, not you.
Listen and show you understand: 'I understand this is frustrating.'
Offer a solution. If you cannot fix it, call your manager.
Afterwards, take a breath and move on.
days.task: Practise staying calm with a friend playing a difficult guest.
days.challenge: Write three calm phrases you can use with upset guests.

quiz.q: What should you do first with a difficult guest?
quiz.explain: Staying calm and listening is the first step.

quiz.q: Why not take it personally?
options: The guest is unhappy with the situation, not with you
quiz.explain: Most upset guests are unhappy about a problem, not about you.

quiz.q: When should you call your manager?
options: If you cannot fix the problem yourself
quiz.explain: If you cannot fix it, a manager can help.

days.title: Hotel Front Office: More Than Check-In
days.goal: Learn the other jobs at a hotel front desk.

video.title: Hotel & Restaurant Problem Handling | Guest Complaints & Service Recovery

steps: Answer phone calls politely and take messages clearly.
Help guests with directions, taxis, and local places.
Handle check-out: give the bill, take payment, and thank the guest.
Keep the front desk tidy and organised.
Know your hotel: rooms, prices, breakfast times, and Wi-Fi.
days.task: Practise answering a phone call as a receptionist.
days.challenge: Write a check-out checklist.

quiz.q: What does a front desk worker do besides check-in?
options: Answer calls, help guests, handle check-out, and keep the desk tidy
quiz.explain: Front desk work covers calls, guest help, check-out, and keeping the desk tidy.

quiz.q: Why know your hotel well?
options: So you can answer guest questions
quiz.explain: Guests ask about rooms, prices, and services. You must know the answers.

quiz.q: What happens at check-out?
options: You give the bill, take payment, and thank the guest
quiz.explain: Check-out means giving the bill, taking payment, and thanking the guest.

days.title: Personalised Service: Make Guests Feel Special
days.goal: Give each guest a personal touch.

video.title: HOW TO: Welcome a guest at your hotel

steps: Remember returning guests and their likes.
Greet regulars by name.
Note special days: birthdays, honeymoons, and anniversaries.
Offer a small surprise: a free drink or a kind note.
Ask guests what they need, not just what they want.
days.task: Write a list of ways to personalise service.
days.challenge: Practise greeting a returning guest by name.

quiz.q: Why remember returning guests?
options: It makes them feel valued and known
quiz.explain: Remembering guests makes them feel special and brings them back.

quiz.q: What is a small surprise you can offer?
options: A free drink or a kind note
quiz.explain: A small surprise shows care and makes a visit memorable.

quiz.q: Why note special days?
options: So you can celebrate with the guest
quiz.explain: Celebrating a birthday or honeymoon makes the stay special.

days.title: Teamwork in Hospitality
days.goal: Work well with your team.

video.title: Hotel & Restaurant Problem Resolution | Handle Complaints & Win Back Guest Trust

steps: Help others when you are free, even if it is not your job.
Share information: tell the kitchen about allergies and special requests.
Be on time. Late staff make the whole team suffer.
Speak kindly to your team. A happy team serves happy guests.
Thank your team after a busy shift.
days.task: Practise sharing information with a teammate.
days.challenge: Write three ways you can help your team this week.

quiz.q: Why help others when you are free?
quiz.explain: Helping teammates keeps service fast and smooth.

quiz.q: Why share allergy information with the kitchen?
options: So the kitchen cooks safe food
quiz.explain: The kitchen must know about allergies to cook safely.

quiz.q: Why be on time?
options: Late staff make the whole team suffer
quiz.explain: One late person can slow the whole team.

days.title: Week 2 Project: Handle a Difficult Day
days.goal: Handle a busy day with complaints and difficult guests.

video.title: How to Handle Hotel Guest Complaints | 4 Essential Front Office Lessons

steps: Greet every guest warmly, even when busy.
Serve food correctly and check back often.
Handle at least one complaint calmly and well.
Help a teammate who is struggling.
At the end, write what went well and what to improve.
days.task: Run a busy service day for friends or family as guests.
days.challenge: Handle a staged complaint and win the guest back.

quiz.q: Why greet warmly even when busy?
options: Guests notice when you are too busy to care
quiz.explain: A warm greeting matters most when you are busy.

quiz.q: Why help a struggling teammate?
quiz.explain: Helping a teammate helps every guest.

quiz.q: Why write what went well?
options: So you learn and improve next time
quiz.explain: Writing lessons down turns a hard day into learning.

project.title: Handle a Difficult Day
project.brief: Run a busy service day with a complaint handled well.
checks: Guests greeted warmly, even when busy
Food served correctly and checked on
Day reviewed: what went well, what to improve

days.title: Body Language: What Guests See
days.goal: Use good body language with guests.

video.title: Rapport Hospitality Customer Service Demo: How to Handle a Frustrated Hotel Guest

steps: Stand up straight. Do not slouch.
Smile. Guests can see a smile and hear it on the phone.
Make eye contact when you greet and listen.
Do not cross your arms. It looks closed and unfriendly.
Move calmly. Rushing looks stressed.
days.task: Practise greeting a friend with good body language.
days.challenge: Ask a friend what your body language says.

quiz.q: Why stand up straight?
quiz.explain: Good posture looks professional and confident.

quiz.q: Why not cross your arms?
quiz.explain: Crossed arms look closed and unwelcoming.

quiz.q: Why make eye contact?
options: It shows you are listening and you care
quiz.explain: Eye contact shows attention and care.

days.title: Phone Skills for Hospitality
days.goal: Answer the phone like a professional.

video.title: How to Handle Restaurant Complaints

steps: Answer within three rings if you can.
Greet with your name and the hotel or restaurant name.
Speak clearly and slowly. Smile: guests can hear it.
Write down messages and repeat them back.
Thank the caller and say goodbye warmly.
days.task: Practise answering a phone call as a receptionist.
days.challenge: Write a phone greeting you can use at work.

quiz.q: How fast should you answer the phone?
options: Within three rings if you can
quiz.explain: Answering fast shows you care about the caller.

quiz.q: What should your greeting include?
options: Your name and the hotel or restaurant name
quiz.explain: A greeting with your name and the business name sounds professional.

quiz.q: Why repeat messages back?
quiz.explain: Repeating a message stops mistakes.

days.title: Upselling: Help Guests Choose More
days.goal: Suggest extras that guests will enjoy.

video.title: Complaint Handling

steps: Upselling means suggesting something extra that fits the guest.
Suggest a drink with a meal, or a dessert after it.
Know your menu well so your suggestions are good.
Never push. If the guest says no, smile and move on.
Upselling helps the guest enjoy more and helps the business earn more.
days.task: Practise suggesting a dessert to a friend after a meal.
days.challenge: List three upselling ideas for a restaurant.

quiz.q: What is upselling?
options: Suggesting something extra that fits the guest
quiz.explain: Upselling suggests an extra that the guest will enjoy.

quiz.q: Why know the menu well for upselling?
quiz.explain: Good suggestions come from knowing the menu.

quiz.q: What if the guest says no?
quiz.explain: Never push. A polite 'no' is fine.

days.title: Cultural Awareness: Serve Everyone Well
days.goal: Serve guests from different cultures with respect.

video.title: Silver Service Training

steps: Learn a few greetings in other languages.
Respect different food rules: some guests do not eat pork or beef.
Ask, do not assume, what a guest wants.
Be patient with guests who speak another language.
Treat every guest with the same care and respect.
days.task: Learn three greetings in another language.
days.challenge: Write a list of common food rules to respect.

quiz.q: Why learn greetings in other languages?
quiz.explain: A greeting in a guest's language shows respect and care.

quiz.q: Why ask instead of assuming?
options: Assuming can offend or get it wrong
quiz.explain: Asking shows respect and stops mistakes.

quiz.q: Why be patient with language differences?
options: Patience helps guests feel safe and understood
quiz.explain: Patience with language makes every guest feel welcome.

days.title: Feedback: Ask and Learn
days.goal: Ask guests for feedback and use it.

video.title: How to Service Food & Beverages | Restaurants | Hotels | Waiter | Fine Dining Training Video

steps: Ask at the end: 'How was everything today?'
Listen to the answer. Do not argue.
Thank guests for feedback, good or bad.
Share feedback with your team.
Fix what guests mention most often.
days.task: Practise asking a friend for feedback after serving them.
days.challenge: Write down three pieces of feedback and what you will change.

quiz.q: When should you ask for feedback?
options: At the end of the visit
quiz.explain: Asking at the end catches the whole visit.

quiz.q: Why thank guests for bad feedback?
options: Bad feedback shows you what to fix
quiz.explain: Bad feedback is the most useful. It shows what to improve.

quiz.q: Why share feedback with your team?
options: So the whole team can improve
quiz.explain: Sharing feedback helps the whole team get better.

days.title: Hospitality Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest service mistakes.

video.title: How to Handle Customer Complaints in Your Restaurant?

steps: Forgot an order? Apologise, fix it fast, and offer something extra.
Served the wrong dish? Replace it at once and say sorry.
Guest waited too long? Apologise and offer a free drink.
Was rude by accident? Say sorry sincerely and move on.
Write down each mistake and fix.
days.task: Fix one service mistake you have made.
days.challenge: Write a list of three mistakes and how you would fix them.

quiz.q: What do you do if you forgot an order?
options: Apologise, fix it fast, and offer something extra
quiz.explain: A fast fix and something extra can save the visit.

quiz.q: What do you do if a guest waited too long?
options: Apologise and offer a free drink
quiz.explain: An apology and a free drink show you care.

quiz.q: Why write mistakes down?
options: So you learn and do not repeat them
quiz.explain: Writing mistakes down helps you learn from them.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Five-Star Service Day
days.goal: Deliver five-star service for a full day.

video.title: Hotel & Restaurant Problem Handling | Guest Complaints & Service Recovery

steps: Greet every guest warmly and by name if you know it.
Serve food correctly and check back often.
Personalise the service: remember likes and special days.
Handle any complaint calmly and win the guest back.
Ask for feedback and thank every guest.
days.task: Run a five-star service day for friends or family.
days.challenge: Ask guests to rate the service and say what made it five-star.

quiz.q: What makes service five-star?
options: Warm greetings, correct service, personal touches, and quick fixes
quiz.explain: Five-star service is warm, correct, personal, and quick to fix problems.

quiz.q: Why personalise service?
quiz.explain: Personal touches make guests feel valued.

quiz.q: Why ask guests to rate the service?
options: So you know what made it five-star
quiz.explain: Ratings tell you what to keep doing.

project.title: Deliver a Five-Star Service Day
project.brief: Serve guests with five-star care for a full day.
checks: Guests greeted warmly and by name
Food served correctly and checked on

days.title: Check-Out and Goodbye
days.goal: Check guests out warmly at a hotel.

video.title: HOW TO: Welcome a guest at your hotel

steps: Greet the guest and ask how their stay was.
Give the bill and explain each charge.
Take payment and give a receipt.
Ask if they need help with bags or a taxi.
Thank them and invite them back.
days.task: Practise a check-out with a friend playing the guest.
days.challenge: Write a check-out checklist.

quiz.q: What should you ask at check-out?
quiz.explain: Asking about the stay shows you care and catches problems.

quiz.q: Why explain each charge on the bill?
options: So the guest understands what they are paying for
quiz.explain: Clear bills stop arguments and build trust.

quiz.q: Why invite guests back?
quiz.explain: An invitation to return keeps guests loyal.

days.title: Loyalty: Keep Guests Coming Back
days.goal: Build loyalty so guests return again and again.

video.title: Hotel & Restaurant Problem Resolution | Handle Complaints & Win Back Guest Trust

steps: Remember regular guests and what they like.
Offer a small reward for repeat visits: a free drink or a discount.
Keep in touch: message regulars about new menus or events.
Ask regulars what they would like to see.
Treat every visit as if it is their first and their best.
days.task: Write a loyalty plan for a small hotel or restaurant.
days.challenge: List three rewards you could offer regular guests.

quiz.q: Why remember regular guests?
options: It makes them feel valued and brings them back
quiz.explain: Remembering regulars builds loyalty.

quiz.q: What reward can you offer regulars?
options: A free drink or a discount
quiz.explain: A small reward thanks regulars and brings them back.

quiz.q: Why ask regulars what they want?
options: So you can offer what they will buy
quiz.explain: Asking regulars tells you what will keep them coming.

days.title: Your Signature Service Style
days.goal: Find the service style that suits you best.

video.title: How to Handle Hotel Guest Complaints | 4 Essential Front Office Lessons

steps: Some people are warm and chatty. Others are calm and quiet. Both can be great.
Be yourself, but always be polite and kind.
Learn from great servers you have met.
Practise your style every day until it feels natural.
Ask guests what they liked about your service.
days.task: Write down your service style in one sentence.
days.challenge: Serve a meal using your style and ask for feedback.

quiz.q: What is a service style?
options: The way you serve: warm, calm, chatty, or quiet
quiz.explain: Your service style is the way you serve guests.

quiz.q: Why be yourself?
options: Guests can tell when you are real
quiz.explain: Real, warm service feels better than a fake smile.

quiz.q: Why ask guests what they liked?
quiz.explain: Guest feedback shows your strengths.

days.title: Hospitality Career: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward a hospitality job.

video.title: Rapport Hospitality Customer Service Demo: How to Handle a Frustrated Hotel Guest

steps: Pick a role: server, receptionist, or front desk agent.
Learn the skills in this course and practise them.
Write a simple CV with your skills and experience.
Apply to hotels and restaurants near you.
At interviews, smile, be polite, and show you care about guests.
days.task: Write a simple CV for a hospitality job.
days.challenge: Practise answering interview questions with a friend.

quiz.q: What should a hospitality CV show?
options: Your skills, experience, and care for guests
quiz.explain: A CV should show your skills and your care for guests.

quiz.q: Why practise interview questions?
options: So you answer clearly and confidently
quiz.explain: Practice makes you calm and clear at interviews.

quiz.q: What matters most at a hospitality interview?
options: A smile, politeness, and care for guests
quiz.explain: A smile and care for guests matter most in hospitality.

days.title: Keeping Records: Guests and Feedback
days.goal: Keep simple records of guests and feedback.

video.title: How to Handle Restaurant Complaints

steps: Write down regular guests and what they like.
Write down feedback, good and bad.
Note complaints and how you fixed them.
Share records with your team so everyone knows.
Use records to improve service every week.
days.task: Start a simple guest record book today.
days.challenge: Write down three pieces of feedback and what you changed.

quiz.q: Why write down what regulars like?
options: So every staff member can serve them well
quiz.explain: Shared records help the whole team serve regulars well.

quiz.q: Why note complaints and fixes?
options: So you learn and do not repeat mistakes
quiz.explain: Complaint records help you fix problems for good.

quiz.q: Why share records with your team?
options: So everyone can serve guests well
quiz.explain: Shared records make the whole team better.

days.title: Service on Busy Days
days.goal: Keep service good even when it is busy.

video.title: Complaint Handling

steps: Greet every guest, even if briefly, when you are busy.
Work as a team: help each other.
Tell guests honestly if there is a wait.
Keep calm. Guests copy your mood.
After a busy day, thank your team.
days.task: Practise serving on a busy day with friends as guests.
days.challenge: Write three tips for busy days.

quiz.q: What should you do when busy?
quiz.explain: A quick greeting matters most when you are busy.

quiz.q: Why tell guests honestly about a wait?
options: Honest waits are easier to accept
quiz.explain: Guests accept an honest wait better than a surprise.

quiz.q: Why keep calm on busy days?
quiz.explain: A calm team makes guests feel calm too.

days.title: Hospitality Trends: What Guests Want Now
days.goal: Learn what guests want today.

video.title: Silver Service Training

steps: Guests want fast Wi-Fi and easy check-in.
Guests want healthy food choices and clear menus.
Guests want staff who remember them.
Guests want to book and pay on their phones.
Ask your guests what they want and offer it.
days.task: Ask three people what they want from a hotel or restaurant.
days.challenge: List three trends you will use in your service.

quiz.q: What do guests want now?
options: Fast Wi-Fi, easy check-in, and healthy choices
quiz.explain: Today's guests want fast Wi-Fi, easy check-in, and healthy food.

quiz.q: Why offer phone booking and payment?
options: Guests like it fast and easy
quiz.explain: Phone booking and payment are fast and easy for guests.

quiz.q: Why ask guests what they want?
options: So you can offer what they will buy
quiz.explain: Asking guests tells you what to offer.

days.title: Revision: The Hospitality Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: How to Service Food & Beverages | Restaurants | Hotels | Waiter | Fine Dining Training Video

steps: Greet a guest from memory, without help.
Serve a meal correctly from memory.
Handle a complaint calmly from memory.
Name the steps of service.
List your three strongest skills and one to improve.
days.task: Serve a full meal from memory, no notes.
days.challenge: Teach one hospitality skill from this course to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What are the steps of service?
options: Greet, seat, order, serve, check back, clear, thank
quiz.explain: Service is greet, seat, order, serve, check back, clear, and thank.

quiz.q: Why serve from memory?
options: It proves you really know the steps
quiz.explain: Serving without notes shows the skills are truly learned.

quiz.q: Why teach a skill to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Service Day
days.goal: Plan your capstone service day.

video.title: How to Handle Customer Complaints in Your Restaurant?

steps: Choose your capstone: a full service day for guests.
Write the plan: greeting, serving, checking back, and goodbye.
Prepare for a complaint and a difficult guest.
Check you have everything you need.
Do a trial run of the hardest part if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone task today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone show?
options: Everything you learned: greeting, serving, complaints, and feedback
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why prepare for a complaint?
options: So you handle it calmly when it happens
quiz.explain: Preparing for complaints means you stay calm when they happen.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real day
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Five-Star Host: A Full Day of Great Service
capstone.brief: Deliver a full day of five-star service to real guests: warm greetings, correct table service, personal touches, calm complaint handling, and a warm goodbye. Collect feedback and write a short report on the day.
checks: Guests greeted warmly and by name where known
Checked back within 2 minutes of serving
Complaints handled calmly and fixed, if any
deliverables: A photo or note of your service day setup
Your service plan: greeting, serving, checking back, goodbye
Your complaint-handling guide written in your own words
Guest feedback collected on the day
A short report on what went well and what you will improve next
